sources.inspection_note: Read lines 22–90: no_grad disables gradient recording for ordinary operations and restores prior grad state at context exit. The factory exception is explicit. This supports using zero_ inside the context; it is not an optimizer update or a training event.

sources.title: PyTorch default norm original implementation
sources.authority_reason: Original PyTorch project source at the installed wheel's git revision; downloaded bytes exactly match the installed module.
sources.inspection_note: Read norm lines 1734–1807 and CPU dispatch lines 1841–1874. The default p='fro', dim=None computes over all elements, and this strided CPU route uses vector_norm with p=2. For (1,8) this is exactly the eight-component L2 length. The legacy norm API is deprecated in the official text, but supported in this installed execution; no change was required to verify the lesson.

sources.title: Independent original-fence and affine control execution
Affine difference and interpretation boundary
sources.details: For f(x)=xW^T+b, f(0)-f(1)=-1W^T: bias cancels; W=0 gives identical b for every input. The row [1,2,0,0] with b=.5 gives .5 and 3.5. Difference norm over one eight-component vector is sqrt(sum(delta_j^2)), dimensionless, with no accuracy denominator. Two arbitrary feature vectors contain no red/blue labels or generated answer criterion, so nonzero difference cannot establish semantic correctness. The text, red-image and blue-image cases are controlled diagnostic goals; text failure blocks attributing all subsequent errors solely to the connector, while text success does not alone identify a unique image-side cause.
